_comment: Story events (data/stories.json): each has a story and an act. Act 1 is the hook; the rest come only through chains (or a battle's won/lost). Every choice must go on to the story's next event, into a fight with won/lost events, or to an ending. The debt story's hook is want_debt (data/events/wants.json); the castaway's is queued when you maroon someone you knew (Wants.part).

brother_knife.title: A brother's knife
brother_knife.text: In an alley off the square in {port}, someone steps out of a doorway with a knife and your name on their lips. {avenger}. You took their house, their savings and their brother.

choices.result: It's over quickly. You leave {avenger} bleeding in the gutter for the watch. They'll live, and they'll remember.
choices.fail_result: You drive {avenger} off, but not before the blade finds your ribs.

choices.result: {avenger} weeps, and drops the knife, and lets you talk. You leave them a purse and the name of your ship.
choices.fail_result: {avenger} isn't listening. You get away with a cut on your arm.

choices.text: Throw them a purse and walk away (100 gold)
choices.result: {avenger} throws the purse back at you. It splits on the cobbles, and children come running for the coins.

brother_letter.title: A letter from {town}
brother_letter.text: A letter finds you in {port}, in a careful, schoolroom hand. {avenger} has thought about what you said in the alley. The church roof in {town} is still open to the rain. Their brother is buried under it.

choices.text: Send money for the roof (300 gold)
choices.result: You send the money with a letter you rewrite four times.
A reply comes a month later: one line. 'I don't forgive you. But I'm done.'
choices.fail_result: Your words come out wrong on the page. You know it as soon as the letter's gone.

choices.result: The letter curls up in the galley fire. You don't think about it again, for a while.

brother_handbills.title: Your name on the walls
brother_handbills.text: Handbills on every wall in {port}: your name, your ship, and a reward for proof of your death. They're signed {avenger}, of {town}. Someone has sold a house to pay for this.

choices.text: Tear them down and find out who's posting them
choices.result: A frightened printer tells you everything: the money came through a pirate hunter, and the hunter has already sailed. Now you know what to look for.
choices.fail_result: Nobody will tell you anything. The bills go back up as fast as you tear them down.

choices.text: Send word to {avenger}: settle it at dawn, the two of us
choices.result: You leave a letter at the printer's. If {avenger} wants you, they know where to find you: the beach below {town}.
Let them print what they like.

brother_hunter.title: A sail astern
brother_hunter.text: A fast sloop has been on your quarter for two days, never closing, never falling back. Her master is a pirate hunter, paid in {town} silver: {avenger}'s silver.

choices.result: You wear ship and run out your guns.
The hunter takes your gold, and as a courtesy tells you where {avenger} will be waiting: the beach below {town}, any dawn you like.

brother_dawn.title: Dawn below {town}
brother_dawn.text: {avenger} is waiting on the beach below {town} at first light, with a borrowed sword and two seconds who look sorry to be there. Half the town is watching from the dunes.

choices.result: Three passes, a feint, and it's done. The town walks home in silence.
choices.fail_result: You're on your back in the wet sand with {avenger}'s point at your throat. A long moment. Then they throw the sword into the sea and walk away.

choices.text: Lay down your sword and pay for what you burned (500 gold)
choices.result: You put your sword on the sand and the purse beside it. The crowd on the dunes doesn't know what to do. Neither does {avenger}.

choices.text: Have your gunners settle it from the boat
choices.result: A swivel gun barks from the longboat. The seconds run.

brother_avenged.title: {avenger} on the quay
brother_avenged.text: Word reaches you: when the hunter brought your beaten ship into port, {avenger} was on the quay to watch. They didn't say a word. They just looked at you for a long time, and then went home to {town}.

choices.result: Perhaps that's fair.
You say it out loud, so the crew hear. It doesn't make you feel better.

dying_pirate.title: An old pirate's last words
dying_pirate.text: In a tavern back room an old buccaneer is dying of the drink. He grips your sleeve: 'Silver, Captain. Silver from the Panama raid, buried on a cay off {port}. I never went back for it.' At the next table, {listener} is very carefully not listening.

choices.text: Sit with him and hear it all
choices.result: He dies before dawn. You have a bearing, a landmark, a number of paces. When you look up, the next table is empty.

choices.text: Buy him a last bottle and leave him be
choices.result: He dies happy, if not rich.

dying_pirate_cay.title: The cay off {port}
dying_pirate_cay.text: You anchor off {port}, row to the low cay the old man described, and find the blasted tree he swore by. The sand beneath it has been turned over, not long ago.

choices.result: The old man's paces lead to a second hole the diggers missed: two chests of silver, black with tarnish. The rest is gone. Someone else heard him.
choices.fail_result: Nothing but empty holes and an iron chest lid, kicked aside. Someone else heard him.

choices.text: Take the whole crew ashore and turn the cay over
choices.result: Three days and every hand with a spade. You find what the first diggers missed, and the marks of a boat that was here a week ago.

silver_listener.title: Tarnished silver
silver_listener.text: In the tavern, {listener} is buying rounds for the whole room, and paying with silver bars black with tarnish. They see you come in, and the smile goes.

choices.result: Up against the wall, {listener} tells you everything. They couldn't carry it all: their friends sail tomorrow to fetch the rest from where they hid it.
choices.fail_result: {listener} slips out of the back while your bosun is still getting up off the floor. They'll warn the others.

choices.result: {listener} spits on a palm and shakes yours. Their friends have the rest, and they don't know {listener} has changed sides.
choices.fail_result: {listener} laughs in your face. You'll have to take it the hard way.

choices.result: It was a dying man's story. Let somebody have the luck of it.

silver_race.title: A sloop low in the water
silver_race.text: There she is: a sloop beating out of a cay's lee, sitting low in the water. The old man's silver is in her hold.

choices.result: All sail. She's heavy, and you're not.
You watch her out of sight.

silver_hold.title: The old man's silver
silver_hold.text: Her hold is half full of tarnished bars and broken church plate, stamped with the arms of Panama. The crew are already counting.

choices.text: Share it out fair, by the articles
choices.result: Every hand gets a bar to hold. Some of them kiss it.
You take the best of it. The crew see you do it.

silver_outrun.title: Hull down
silver_outrun.text: The sloop is hull down on the horizon, and the old man's silver with her.

choices.result: The crew curse it with you.

debt_interest.title: Interest
debt_interest.text: A notice nailed up on the quay at {port}: the debt of {who}, now six hundred gold with interest, has been bought by a man who collects for the courts. He has collected before. {who} has gone very quiet.

choices.result: Twice what it was. The collector counts it twice too.

choices.text: Post a guard on {who}, and go to {town} to settle it
choices.result: The collector's men come in the night, and find your bosun waiting with a cudgel. You'll settle this in {town}, face to face.
choices.fail_result: In the morning {who}'s hammock is empty, and there are marks on the rail where they were dragged over it.

choices.result: The collector thanks you. Nobody else does.

debt_house.title: The counting house
debt_house.text: The counting house in {town} smells of ink and sealing wax. The lender sits behind a desk with two large men behind him and {who}'s debt in a ledger in front of him.

choices.result: The lender strikes the line through with a flourish.

choices.text: Make the debt the ship's: paid from the next voyages
choices.result: The lender likes a debtor with a ship. The crew are less pleased: it comes out of the wages.
choices.fail_result: The lender wants coin, not promises. Come back when you have it.

choices.result: The lender's men take one look at your boarding party and find somewhere else to be. The ledger burns very nicely.
choices.fail_result: It comes to fists and then knives, and the watch arrives before the smoke clears. You get out, and the ledger doesn't.

choices.result: You came all this way to do it. The crew won't forget that either.

castaway_word.title: A face from the sandbar
castaway_word.text: A turtler in {port} tells a story over his rum: a castaway, taken off a sandbar more dead than alive. Thin as a rope, burnt black, and asking every captain in port about the {ship}. It's {who}, the one you marooned.

choices.text: Find them and make it right (200 gold)
choices.result: {who} takes the money and doesn't thank you. But the hate goes out of their eyes, a little.
choices.fail_result: {who} takes the money, and spends it on a ship.

choices.text: Offer them their old berth back
choices.result: A long silence. Then {who} picks up their sea chest.

choices.text: Pay someone to finish the job
choices.result: The man you pay comes back without his ear. {who} has friends now.
Talk is cheap.

castaway_ship.title: Colours dipped, insolently
castaway_ship.text: A sloop crosses your bow at long range and dips her colours to you, slow and mocking. Through the glass you can see {who} at her rail, raising a hat.

choices.result: All hands. You'll have them.
You let them go. The crew think you're afraid of them.

castaway_reckoning.title: Waiting off the cape
castaway_reckoning.text: {who} has been selling what they know: your ship's slow tack, the rotten timber by the stern post, how your gunners load. This morning a ship is waiting for you off the cape, and {who} is aboard her.

choices.result: There's no getting round her.
Every stitch of canvas.

castaway_taken.title: {who} in irons
castaway_taken.text: {who} is brought aboard in irons and stood on the deck where they once stood watch. The crew who sailed with them won't meet their eye.

choices.result: The crew do it. They don't like it.

choices.text: Maroon them again, with a pistol this time
choices.result: A sandbar, a bottle of water, a pistol, one ball.
You strike the irons off yourself and put them in a boat.

castaway_gone.title: Out there still
castaway_gone.text: {who} is gone over the horizon, and every captain in the islands will soon know what they know about your ship.

choices.result: There'll be another day.

pardon_old_friends.title: Old friends
pardon_old_friends.text: {friend} is drinking in the corner of the tavern in {port}, still on the account, still in the old coat. They look up as you come in, and the whole room hears what they call you: turncoat.

choices.text: Sit down and drink with them anyway
choices.result: By the third bottle you're both laughing about the old days. By the fourth, neither of you is.
You hear them laugh behind you all the way to the door.

pardon_commission.title: The commission
pardon_commission.text: The governor's secretary in {port} has a paper for you: a commission to hunt down and bring in {friend}, who has refused the King's mercy. 'You know the haunts, Captain. And a pardon must be earned.'

choices.result: Three hundred in advance, the rest on delivery.
You take the governor's money and send a boy to the old haunt with a message.
The secretary makes a note.

pardon_hunt.title: The old haunts
pardon_hunt.text: You know where {friend} waters, and there's their ship, careened on the beach where the two of you once careened together. They've seen you.

choices.result: Beat to quarters.

choices.text: Let them slip away, and report that you lost them
choices.result: You look the other way while they float her off on the tide.

pardon_taken.title: {friend} in irons
pardon_taken.text: {friend} sits in irons in your hold, the way you'd have sat if you'd been unluckier. 'Remember the Main?' they ask you. You do.

choices.result: You hand them over at the quay. You don't stay for the hanging.

choices.text: Cut their bonds in the night
choices.result: A knife, a boat, a nod. That's all.

pardon_away.title: Away on the tide
pardon_away.text: {friend} beats you off and gets away on the tide. You hear later what they're calling you in Nassau now.

choices.text: Let them call you what they like
choices.result: An old friend is the worst kind of enemy.
